catalog_quote: [p. x, 1.1] There is an additional phoneme of stress, indicated by an acute accent (´) over the vowel, that varies dialectically though it usually occurs on the next to the last syllable. ... [p. xi, 1.2.1] Since stress has a low contrastive function, it will be marked only when it causes a difference in meaning between two words, for example: pahid ‘wipe’ pahíd ‘shrub’ / salà ‘small cut’ salâ ‘sin’ ... [p. xiii, 2.1.6 Stress shift] With suffixation the stress shifts to the new penult of the word, for example: kágat ‘bite’ + -en = kagáten ‘bite something’ / lébeng ‘bury’ + -anan = lebengánan ‘grave’ ... [p. viii] Although there are some minimal pairs where stress is contrastive, this contrast is only indicated in the entry word. Once the word appears in a sentence or is affixed, the stress rules apply so there is no need to indicate it.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every quoted passage is present verbatim at the cited pages of the held Post & Gardner 1992 PDF (PDF pp. 10, 12, 13, 15), diacritics verified on the page image. (2) Deciding source is a 1992 SIL grammar sketch inside the dictionary, by the language's long-term primary fieldworker; Glottolog lists no fuller grammar or phonology, and the one later phonology article (Hermocilla-Borres 2018, fetched sources) covers segments only and is silent on stress; no instrumental or JIPA work exists per web search. (3) The coding 'lexical, non-strict, penult default, shift to new penult under suffixation' matches the source exactly (phonemic stress with minimal pairs pahid/pahíd, salà/salâ; 'usually' penultimate; low contrastive function). Nothing found contradicts it; Peng & Billings 2006 and the Rosetta excerpt merely restate P&G. Remaining unheld items (Atherton 1953, 4 pp; Borres 2017 diss

sources.citation: Peng, Adam & Loren Billings. 2006. Binukid pronominal clisis. Paper presented at 10-ICAL, Puerto Princesa. 25 pp.
sources.quote: 'a grave accent (`) is marked over a word- or syllable-final vowel letter to indicate a following glottal stop ... whereas an acute accent (´) is used to disambiguate stress. If stress is final and a glottal stop is present, then a circumflex accent (ˆ) is used.' Restates Post & Gardner; treats stress as needing lexical disambiguation.
